Use `snl batch check` to preflight a dependent multi-entity change set without writing.

### Availability
This Entry is a normative product contract. The command is implemented only when its canonical path appears in machine-readable `snl --help`; absence means planned and unavailable, never silently emulated through a different command.


### Command path
`batch/check` is the canonical transport-neutral command. The intended shell spelling is `snl batch check`. Current availability is advertised by machine-readable `snl --help`; an Agent/MCP adapter submits the same operation object instead of reconstructing shell text.

### Operation request
```json
{"protocol":"snl.operation/v1","command":"batch/check","root":"/absolute/workspace","arguments":{"operations":[]}}
```
Every adapter accepts exactly this semantic request. Unknown argument keys are rejected. The CLI accepts `--root` and `--json` globally and emits one complete JSON document followed by a newline. Schema, syntax/semantic, and workspace-reference diagnostics remain distinguishable.

### Success result
A successful call exits `0` and returns `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":true,"command":"batch/check","data":{},"diagnostics":[]}`. `data` contains `normalizedOperations`, the exact `checkedDigest`, `expectedWorkspaceRevision`, and stable-code diagnostics. `ok:true` means no error-severity diagnostic; the two opaque tokens authorize only this normalized batch against this workspace snapshot.

### Failure and exit semantics
Domain rejection (invalid data, not-found, conflict, or validation errors) exits `1`. Invocation, input I/O, unsupported workspace/schema, lock acquisition, and runtime failures exit `2`. Failure stdout under `--json` is exactly one `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":false,"command":"batch/check","error":{"code":"<stable-code>","message":"<actionable text>","details":{},"retryable":false}}`; no stack trace or prose contaminates stdout.

### State and concurrency
Read-only. It must not create temp files inside `.SNL_Doc`, acquire a writer lock, or repair the draft. The checked digest commits to the normalized operation sequence and the expected workspace revision commits to every authority read by preflight. Revisions, cursors, checked digests, and workspace revisions are opaque tokens. Repeated calls against unchanged bytes return equivalent semantic results.
